overview: From 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-18, ethereum-optimism/specs had 4 new PRs (2 merged), 0 new issues, and 18 active contributors.

topIssues.title: SDM: make it clear that violating refund(i) <= evmGasUsed(i) invalidates the entire block
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
If a sequencer actually broadcasts an invalid postexec tx, by trying to refund too much gas, verifiers will reject the entire block.

Not to be confused with sequencer policies / safeguards (it can prevent itself from doing the above by catching buggy policies on the fly).

topPRs.title: jovian: Correct the four upgrade-deposit intent strings
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The Jovian L1Block and GasPriceOracle upgrade deposits publish source hashes that no chain produces.

The generator built each intent string from the Solidity contract name, for example `Jovian: GasPriceOracle Deployment`. The intent for these two contracts spaces the words, as Ecotone, Fjord and Isthmus do. The intent fixes the source hash, so the published hashes are wrong. The fifth Jovian deposit, `Jovian: Gas Price Oracle Set Jovian`, was written by hand and was already correct.

OP Mainnet block 144546212 activates Jovian. Its upgrade deposits carry the four source hashes in this change:

| Intent | sourceHash |
|---|---|
| `Jovian: L1 Block Deployment` | `0xbb1a656f65401240fac3db12e7a79ebb954b11e62f7626eb11691539b798d3bf` |
| `Jovian: L1 Block Proxy Update` | `0xf3275f829340521028f9ad5bce4ecb1c64a45d448794effa2a77674627338e76` |
| `Jovian: Gas Price Oracle Deployment` | `0x239b7021a6c2cf3a918481242bbb5a9499057f24501539467536c691bb133962` |
| `Jovian: Gas Price Oracle Proxy Update` | `0xa70c60aa53b8c1c0d52b39b1e901e7d7c09f7819595cb24048a6bb1983b401ff` |

Both implementations use the same intent strings, pinned at `ethereum-optimism/optimism@c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb`:

- op-node: [`jovian_upgrade_transactions.go#L16-L17`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/op-node/rollup/derive/jovian_upgrade_transactions.go#L16-L17) and [`#L25-L26`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/op-node/rollup/derive/jovian_upgrade_transactions.go#L25-L26)
- kona: [`jovian.rs#L35`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/rust/kona/crates/protocol/hardforks/src/jovian.rs#L35), [`#L40`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/rust/kona/crates/protocol/hardforks/src/jovian.rs#L40), [`#L45`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/rust/kona/crates/protocol/hardforks/src/jovian.rs#L45), [`#L51`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/rust/kona/crates/protocol/hardforks/src/jovian.rs#L51)

`gen_predeploy_docs.py` takes a new `--intent-name` option. It defaults to `--contract-name`, so the other fork configurations do not change. Only the intent strings use it. The section headings, the deployment addresses and the bytecode file names keep the contract name.

topPRs.title: lagoon: state that an SDM refund above evmGasUsed invalidates the block
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

Closes #955.

`sdm.md` says `refund(i)` MUST be `<= evmGasUsed(i)`, and #952 names that bound as one of only two consensus constraints on refunds. But the spec never says what a violation does. "Invalidates the block" is stated only for the envelope rules and for settlement underflow. The bound is not in the numbered validity rules, because checking it needs execution. **Producer and Verifier** lists what a verifier enforces without it. A reader could take the MUST as "clamp the refund" or "ignore the entry", and either would split consensus with a client that rejects the block.

The settlement underflow rule does not cover this case. The debited balances (base fee vault, operator fee vault, block beneficiary) include fees accumulated over earlier transactions and blocks. So a refund above `evmGasUsed(i)` would typically settle with no underflow, paying those accumulated fees out to the sender.

## What changes

All edits are in `specs/protocol/lagoon/sdm.md`.

- **Canonical Gas:** if `refund(i) > evmGasUsed(i)` for any transaction, the entire block is invalid. A verifier MUST NOT clamp the refund or skip the entry. The section also notes that the bound is checked during execution, not when the payload is decoded.
- **Application Rules:** the converse of the existing "cannot underflow" sentence does not hold, so the underflow check does not replace the bound.
- **Producer and Verifier:** the verifier bullet now includes the bound. A new sentence says a sequencer MAY guard against a refund policy that breaks the bound (for example by dropping the refund), and that this is producer behavior, not a consensus rule.
- **Security Considerations:** adds an **Excessive refunds** entry.

There is no consensus change. This matches existing behavior: op-reth and kona share the `alloy-op-evm` executor, which rejects the block with `InvalidPostExecPayload` when `refund > evm_gas_used`, checked per transaction before settlement (`test_verifier_rejects_refund_exceeding_evm_gas`). The sequencer-side safeguard is `sanitize_producer_refund` from ethereum-optimism/optimism#22963, which sets an oversized refund to zero.

## Checks

`markdownlint-cli2` and `cspell` pass on `sdm.md`. No headings changed, so the TOC is unaffected.

topPRs.title: lagoon: specify block-level warming as a producer policy with a net refund
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
## Why

The block-level warming policy rebates the gross EIP-2929 surcharge on block-warm accesses. The EIP-3529 refund cap (gas spent / 5) and the EIP-7623 calldata floor both depend on gas spent, so when either binds, part of that surcharge never reached the transaction's gas used:

- **Cap binds:** up to one fifth of the rebate is unbacked. In the audit's example, a transaction is charged 65,324 gas against 105,324 had its block-warm reads been priced transaction-warm.
- **Floor binds:** the whole rebate is unbacked.

These are internal audit findings SDM-M5 and SDM-L10. The spec's only wording on this, "rebate only accesses actually charged the cold price", supports both a gross and a net reading. It also left it unclear whether the policy is a consensus rule at all.

## What changes

- **Gas Refund Semantics** keeps only the consensus rule: clients apply the included refund, subject to the validity rules and `refund(i) <= evmGasUsed(i)`.
- **Refund Policy** (new subsection) states that a refund policy is not a consensus rule. Verifiers don't run it, and a block whose refunds differ from it is still valid.
- **Block-Level Warming Policy** (new subsection) has four parts:
  - *Warmth States:* defines cold, block-warm and transaction-warm, and what is warm from the start of a transaction.
  - *Surcharges:* the per-access amounts (2500 account, 2000 `SLOAD`, 2100 `SSTORE`) and which opcodes they cover.
  - *Refund Amount:* the policy refunds the **net saving**, `evmGasUsed(i) - warmGasUsed(i)`, where `warmGasUsed` recomputes the cap and floor with the surcharges removed. A refund therefore never charges a transaction less than it would have used had its block-warm accesses been priced transaction-warm.
  - *Known Limitations:* non-normative.
- **`evmGasUsed`** is now defined explicitly as after the EIP-3529 cap and the EIP-7623 floor.
- **Producer and Verifier** and **Security Considerations** now point to the policy subsection and repeat that it is guidance for producers.

There is no consensus change. Verifiers behave exactly as before.

Implementation: ethereum-optimism/optimism#23191

## Checks

`markdownlint-cli2`, `doctoc` and `cspell` all pass on `sdm.md`. Five opcode names were added to `words.txt`.

topPRs.title: guaranteed-gas-market: Make the resource limit inclusive
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The pseudocode in "Limiting Guaranteed Gas" rejects a purchase that reaches `MAX_RESOURCE_LIMIT`. The implementation accepts it. This change makes the comparison inclusive.

The `OptimismPortal` is the only implementation of this bound. No client enforces it. References are pinned at `ethereum-optimism/optimism@c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb`:

- [`ResourceMetering.sol#L130-L131`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/ResourceMetering.sol#L130-L131) reverts only when the new total is strictly greater than `maxResourceLimit`.
- [`OptimismPortal2.sol#L730`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/OptimismPortal2.sol#L730) applies the `metered` modifier to `depositTransaction`. That modifier is the only caller.

The prose agrees with the inclusive form. The page sets "a guaranteed gas limit of `MAX_RESOURCE_LIMIT` gas per L1 block", and a limit of N includes N. The stated safety property is that guaranteed gas stays below the L2 block gas limit. [`SystemConfig.sol#L515`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/SystemConfig.sol#L515) enforces that relation inclusively, so a purchase that reaches exactly `maxResourceLimit` still satisfies it.

topPRs.title: deposits: Remove the reference to source-hash domains 3 and 4
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`deposits.md` states that the interop derivation specification introduces two more system deposits, with domains `3` and `4`. Neither domain exists. These two lines are the only mention of either domain in the specification tree. No page defines a preimage for either.

Domain 4 belonged to the optimistic block deposited transaction. #900 deleted that section and replaced the mechanism with Holocene Replacement. `specs/interop/derivation.md` now trims the replacement block "to include only deposit transactions", with no marker transaction.

Domain 3 never shipped. An early interop draft used it for deposit context window transactions. The `CrossL2Inbox` access-list check replaced that design. [`deposit_source.go#L16-L18`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/op-node/rollup/derive/deposit_source.go#L16-L18) records this.

No client uses either domain. The types still exist, but nothing outside their own files and tests calls them:

- [`deposit_source.go#L71-L80`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/op-node/rollup/derive/deposit_source.go#L71-L80)
- [`source.rs#L139-L165`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb/rust/op-alloy/crates/consensus/src/source.rs#L139-L165)

Both references are pinned at `ethereum-optimism/optimism@c93d28340f4c91e42b1a88cfc9e78c3a33093ceb`.

This change does not reserve the two numbers. Neither reached production.

The deleted link was also wrong. From `specs/protocol/deposits.md`, `./derivation.md` resolves to the protocol derivation page, not the interop one.
